# Review pack: The mother of Musa

Notes from the drafter: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

## Story-level uncertainties

- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later works give a name to the mother of Musa and to his sister, and describe where the chest came to rest.
- Hadith to add later: reports about the mother of Musa and the chest, with a named grader for each; none is used here.

## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. What was inspired to her  (`#what-was-inspired-to-her`)

Cited ayat: 20:38-39, 28:7

> **20:38** إِذْ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ
>
> **20:39** أَنِ ٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلتَّابُوتِ فَٱقْذِفِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ فَلْيُلْقِهِ ٱلْيَمُّ بِٱلسَّاحِلِ يَأْخُذْهُ عَدُوٌّ لِّى وَعَدُوٌّ لَّهُۥ وَأَلْقَيْتُ عَلَيْكَ مَحَبَّةً مِّنِّى وَلِتُصْنَعَ عَلَىٰ عَيْنِىٓ

> **28:7** وَأَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰٓ أَنْ أَرْضِعِيهِ فَإِذَا خِفْتِ عَلَيْهِ فَأَلْقِيهِ فِى ٱلْيَمِّ وَلَا تَخَافِى وَلَا تَحْزَنِىٓ إِنَّا رَآدُّوهُ إِلَيْكِ وَجَاعِلُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ

### Claims

**c1** (28:7): God inspired the mother of Musa to nurse him, and, when she feared for him, to cast him into the water.

**c2** (28:7): She was told not to fear and not to grieve, for God would return him to her and make him one of the messengers.

**c3** (20:38-39): God says to Musa that He inspired his mother with what was inspired: to put him in the chest and cast it into the water, so that the water would throw it on the bank, where one who was an enemy to God and to him would take him.

### One-minute summary

God inspired the mother of Musa to nurse him, and, when she feared for him, to cast him into the water [c1]. She was told not to fear or grieve, because God would return him to her [c2].

### Complete story

God inspired the mother of Musa to nurse him, and, when she feared for him, to cast him into the water [c1]. She was told not to fear and not to grieve, for God would return him to her and make him one of the messengers [c2]. God says to Musa that He inspired his mother with what was inspired: to put him in the chest and cast it into the water, so that the water would throw it on the bank, where one who was an enemy to God and to him would take him [c3].

### Deep study

The instruction appears in one passage as an inspiration to nurse and then to cast him out [c1], and in another as putting him in the chest and casting it into the water [c3]. The Arabic for the water, al-yamm, can mean a river or a sea, and the ayat do not say which [c1].

### Kids mode

God told the mother of Musa to nurse him, and, if she was afraid, to put him in the water [c1]. God told her not to be afraid or sad, because He would bring him back to her [c2].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the instruction and the promise of his return are given together [c1][c2].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the mother's name, her age or where she lived.
- Not established: how the inspiration came to her; the ayat do not say whether it was a dream, a voice or another means.
- Not established: how old the child was when she cast him out, or how long she nursed him.
- Not established: which water was meant, or what the chest was made of.

## 2. Found and returned  (`#found-and-returned`)

Cited ayat: 20:40, 28:8, 28:10-13

> **20:40** إِذْ تَمْشِىٓ أُخْتُكَ فَتَقُولُ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ مَن يَكْفُلُهُۥ فَرَجَعْنَٰكَ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّكَ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا فَنَجَّيْنَٰكَ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ وَفَتَنَّٰكَ فُتُونًا فَلَبِثْتَ سِنِينَ فِىٓ أَهْلِ مَدْيَنَ ثُمَّ جِئْتَ عَلَىٰ قَدَرٍ يَٰمُوسَىٰ

> **28:8** فَٱلْتَقَطَهُۥٓ ءَالُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَنًا إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ وَهَٰمَٰنَ وَجُنُودَهُمَا كَانُوا۟ خَٰطِـِٔينَ

> **28:10** وَأَصْبَحَ فُؤَادُ أُمِّ مُوسَىٰ فَٰرِغًا إِن كَادَتْ لَتُبْدِى بِهِۦ لَوْلَآ أَن رَّبَطْنَا عَلَىٰ قَلْبِهَا لِتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
>
> **28:11** وَقَالَتْ لِأُخْتِهِۦ قُصِّيهِ فَبَصُرَتْ بِهِۦ عَن جُنُبٍ وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
>
> **28:12** وَحَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلْمَرَاضِعَ مِن قَبْلُ فَقَالَتْ هَلْ أَدُلُّكُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَهْلِ بَيْتٍ يَكْفُلُونَهُۥ لَكُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُۥ نَٰصِحُونَ
>
> **28:13** فَرَدَدْنَٰهُ إِلَىٰٓ أُمِّهِۦ كَىْ تَقَرَّ عَيْنُهَا وَلَا تَحْزَنَ وَلِتَعْلَمَ أَنَّ وَعْدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (28:8): The family of Fir'awn picked him up, so that he would become an enemy and a source of grief to them, for Fir'awn, Haman and their forces were in error.

**c2** (28:10): The heart of the mother of Musa became empty, and she would almost have revealed him had God not strengthened her heart, so that she would be among the believers.

**c3** (28:11): She told his sister to follow him, and she watched him from a distance, while they did not perceive.

**c4** (28:12, 20:40): God had forbidden him wet-nurses beforehand, and his sister asked whether she might direct them to a household that would take care of him for them and wished him well.

**c5** (28:13, 20:40): God returned him to his mother so that she would be comforted and not grieve, and so that she would know that God's promise is true, though most of them do not know.

### One-minute summary

The family of Fir'awn picked up the child [c1]. The heart of the mother of Musa became empty, and God strengthened it so that she would be among the believers [c2]. His sister watched, and spoke of a household that would take care of him, and God returned him to his mother [c3][c4][c5].

### Complete story

The family of Fir'awn picked him up, so that he would become an enemy and a source of grief to them, for Fir'awn, Haman and their forces were in error [c1]. The heart of the mother of Musa became empty, and she would almost have revealed him had God not strengthened her heart, so that she would be among the believers [c2]. She told his sister to follow him, and she watched him from a distance, while they did not perceive [c3]. God had forbidden him wet-nurses beforehand, and his sister asked whether she might direct them to a household that would take care of him for them and wished him well [c4]. God returned him to his mother so that she would be comforted and not grieve, and so that she would know that God's promise is true, though most of them do not know [c5].

### Deep study

The ayat speak of the mother, the sister and the child without naming them [c3][c5]. The words describing her heart as empty are read in more than one way, as empty of patience or as empty of everything but him [c2].

### Kids mode

The mother of Musa told his sister to follow him [c3]. His sister watched from a distance [c3]. God returned him to his mother, so that she would be comforted and not grieve [c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage describes a mother whose heart God strengthened and to whom God returned her child [c2][c5].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: how the family of Fir'awn picked him up, or where.
- Not established: how long the child was away from his mother.
- Not established: which household took care of him, beyond the words of his sister.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later works give names to the mother and the sister.
